Kling 3.0 cost per second: where it’s cheapest

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

The cheapest Kling 3.0 rate we track is $0.0225/s on Higgsfield Ultra (annual) at 720p, audio not stated, an estimate that assumes you use every credit. The cheapest pay-as-you-go rate is $0.0714/s for Kling 3.0 Standard at 720p on the Higgsfield API. The official Kling API is $0.084/s at 720p without native audio and $0.126/s with it, from Kling’s official API pricing document. Every row below states its tier, resolution, audio, usage assumption, source, and the date it was checked. For Kling’s own plans and credit packs, see Kling AI pricing and credits.

Last checked 2026-11-24. Official pages were re-read Nov 17, 2026, 4:04–4:15 PM ET (1:04–1:15 PM PT). Catalog rows use the date on each row. Affiliate links never change this price order. Every dollar-per-second figure below states its usage assumption, tier, resolution, and audio.

Key takeaways

  • Cheapest if you use every credit. $0.0225/s on Higgsfield Ultra (annual), 720p, audio not stated. Estimated from a $50-a-month plan at Higgsfield’s current sale price.
  • Cheapest pay as you go. $0.0714/s on the Higgsfield API, Kling 3.0 Standard, 720p, audio not stated. At 1080p, Higgsfield API Pro is $0.0962/s.
  • Kling direct. The official API is $0.084/s at 720p without audio and $0.126/s with audio. App credits per clip are not published.
  • Cheapest with audio included. $0.112/s for Kling 3.0 Turbo with native audio at 720p on the official API.
  • Image to video. fal and the Higgsfield API list the same per-second rate for image-to-video as for text-to-video.

Where is Kling 3.0 cheapest in November 2026?

The cheapest Kling 3.0 rate we track is $0.0225 per second on Higgsfield Ultra (annual) at 720p, audio not stated. That is an estimate from the credit plan: $45 a month for 3,000 credits, about 7.5 credits per 5-second clip, and it assumes you use every credit you pay for. With no credits to use up, the cheapest pay-as-you-go rate is $0.0714 per second for Kling 3.0 Standard at 720p on the Higgsfield API, audio not stated. The official Kling API charges $0.084 per second at 720p without native audio and $0.126 with it. The cheapest rate whose vendor page says the clip includes audio is $0.112 per second for Kling 3.0 Turbo with native audio at 720p on the official API. Higgsfield links on this page are affiliate links, and they never change this price order.

    What does Kling 3.0 cost per second?

    It depends on the route. Credit plans run from $0.0225 per second (Higgsfield Ultra annual, 720p, estimate) to more than $0.25 per second at 4K, and each assumes every credit is used. Pay-as-you-go APIs run from $0.0714 per second (Higgsfield API, Standard, 720p) through $0.084 (official Kling API, 720p, no audio), $0.09 (Runway API, Standard, no audio) and $0.112 (fal Pro, audio off), up to $0.42 or more per second at 4K. A 10-second 720p clip without audio is $0.84 on the official API and $0.71 on the Higgsfield API.

    What does Kling AI video cost with audio?

    At 720p and 1080p, native audio raises the per-second price on every route that prices it separately. At 4K, the official API and fal charge $0.42 a second either way. On the official Kling API, 720p is $0.084 per second without audio and $0.126 with it, and Kling 3.0 Turbo with audio is $0.112 at 720p. On fal Pro it is $0.112 with audio off and $0.168 with audio on, or $0.196 with voice control. On the Runway API, Standard is $0.09 without audio and $0.13 with it. Higgsfield’s plan page and the Higgsfield API model pages do not say whether their Kling 3.0 rates include audio, so those rows say not stated. Sources: Kling’s official API pricing document · fal’s Kling 3.0 Pro page · Runway API pricing, read Nov 17, 2026, 4:04–4:15 PM ET (1:04–1:15 PM PT).

    Does Kling AI image to video cost the same as text to video?

    On the pages that state input type, yes. fal’s Kling 3.0 Pro image-to-video mode lists the same $0.112 per second with audio off and $0.168 with audio on as its text-to-video mode, and fal’s Standard image-to-video page lists $0.084 and $0.126. The Higgsfield API model pages list $0.0714 per second at 720p for Standard image-to-video and for Standard text-to-video, and $0.0962 at 1080p for Pro in both modes. The official Kling API table bills Kling 3.0 per second of output and does not list a separate image-to-video price. Higgsfield’s plan page and Runway’s API page give one Kling 3.0 price without naming the input type.

    Sources read Nov 17, 2026, 4:04–4:15 PM ET (1:04–1:15 PM PT): fal’s Kling 3.0 Pro page (its Image to Video (pro) mode) · fal’s Kling 3.0 Standard image-to-video page · Higgsfield API Standard image-to-video page · Higgsfield API Standard text-to-video page · Higgsfield API pricing list, which shows Standard image-to-video as $0.0714–$0.1071 per second and Pro as $0.0962–$0.1443 per second without saying which settings give each end of the range. For free ways to animate a photo, see free image to video AI.

    Is Kling direct cheaper than Higgsfield or fal?

    Not on price. The official Kling API ($0.084 per second at 720p without audio) is undercut by the Higgsfield API at $0.0714, and by credit plans on Higgsfield, Magnific and Krea if you use every credit. It is cheaper than fal Pro ($0.112) and Runway’s Pro variants. The official Kling app sells monthly credits, but Kling does not publish how many credits a Kling 3.0 clip uses, so this page cannot turn an app plan into a cost per second. Higgsfield’s annual plan rows use its current Black Friday sale prices, which its pricing page says end Nov 24, 2026, 7:00 PM ET (4:00 PM PT), unless the sale is extended.

    Kling AI video comes from Kuaishou. Kling sells Kling 3.0 two ways: monthly credits in the Kling app (Kling membership plans) and per-second resource packages on the API (Kling’s official API pricing document), which lists 720p, 1080p, and 4K with or without native audio, plus Kling 3.0 Turbo with native audio. Higgsfield, fal, Runway, Krea, and Magnific resell the same model. Kling’s app plans, first-month prices, and credit packs are in Kling AI pricing and credits, and Higgsfield’s credit math is in Higgsfield pricing explained and is Higgsfield worth it?. Official iPhone and Android apps are compared in AI video generator apps.

    If Higgsfield’s annual sale price ends and Ultra bills at its $129 monthly list price, the same 720p Kling 3.0 math is $0.0645/s (catalog row r112, Ultra monthly), still below the official API’s $0.084/s if you use every credit.

    What is confirmed, and what is not?

    Unknown, and not guessed: how many credits a Kling 3.0 clip uses in the official Kling app, so no app-plan cost per second is shown; whether Higgsfield’s plan rates and Higgsfield API rates include native audio; which settings give the top of the Higgsfield API price range ($0.1071 for Standard image-to-video, $0.1443 for Pro); Krea’s Kling 3.0 resolution; Higgsfield’s annual price after its Black Friday sale ends; and a Replicate Kling 3.0 rate, since none is in our catalog.

    Confirmed Nov 17, 2026, 4:04–4:15 PM ET (1:04–1:15 PM PT) on official pages: the official Kling API rates for Kling 3.0 and Kling 3.0 Turbo; fal’s Pro and Standard rates, including the image-to-video modes; Runway’s Kling 3.0 credits per second; the Higgsfield API Standard 720p and Pro 1080p rates; and Higgsfield’s sale prices and its approximate Kling 3.0 credits per 5-second clip.     What to do next

    • Check the vendor page. Prices and sale prices change without notice. Confirm the current figure on Kling’s official API pricing document, Higgsfield’s pricing page, or fal’s Kling 3.0 Pro page before you buy.
    • Try the calculator. Put your clip length into the credit calculator for a 10-second Kling 3.0 clip to see what your plan really costs when you do not use every credit.
    • Open the model page. Every current Kling 3.0 rate, with its source and date, is on the Kling 3.0 model page.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
